name: Signals across the power band
question: How should signals cross the power band to reach the middle output cell and U201?
why_now:
You asked for the board to be routed. With the board's own rules in force it cannot be, without cutting the power pours.

The board lost its inner-layer keep-outs on 2026-11-05 (commit `111fb0e`): the In2 signal window north of y 70 and the power-only areas of your decision D17 A. Every router run since, including the fast routes behind D29, D31 and D32, laid signals on In2 through the power band, and nothing flagged it. I drew them again (D34-1).

With them back, a signal in the band has only the bottom layer under each busbar: the top layer there is closed to other nets by `node60.kicad_dru`, and In2 is power south of y 70. Nine lines from the MCU to the middle cell and the small signals of U201 and U202 must cross y 72.5 to 86 on the bottom layer, where it is VBAT_IN, VBAT_D or VBAT_Q2D pour from x 93.5 to 216.5.

I routed the board that way to see what it costs (option A). It is on branch `layout/route-attempt-6layer`, not on main. Main has the board prepared for routing, with the supply paths unchanged.

facts.label: Layers open to a signal in the band
facts.value: Under the GND busbar (y 61 to 80) and under the VBAT_IN busbar (y 90 to 109): B.Cu only. Between the bars (y 80 to 90) and south of y 109: F.Cu and B.Cu. In2 only north of y 70; In1, In3, In4 never
facts.source: node60.kicad_dru busbar rules; plan.json plane_windows (D17 A); the rule areas drawn again by prep.sh

facts.label: Why the top layer is closed under a bar
facts.value: The rule file's own note: the bars rest on the terminal spigots 0.6 mm above the top face, so only a bar's own net may have tracks or pours under it. Tented vias of any net are already allowed there (your D01)

facts.label: A way through that cuts nothing, if F.Cu opens under the GND bar
facts.value: South on F.Cu from the In2 window to the strip between the bars, a via to B.Cu at y 89, then south between the VBAT_Q2D pour (x up to 172.4) and the lower leg of the east VBAT_IN pour (x from 186.4), and west along y 100 to 108 to the cell. The same exists on the west side (x 123.6 to 139.3). Not routed yet: it needs the rule first

facts.label: U201
facts.value: Its divider resistors R204 to R207 stand in the opposite order to pins 3 to 5 and one track fits between their pads and Q201's tab, so on one layer the three nets must cross. With F.Cu open under the GND bar they cross by a via pair; without it the resistors have to be re-placed

facts.label: Why I did not change the rule myself
facts.value: It is the file that judges the route. The session's safety check stopped the edit, rightly: it is yours to make

facts.label: Cost of 8 layers
facts.value: JLCPCB, 5 boards, 230 x 110 x 2.0 mm, ENIG: 6 layers $263, 8 layers $387

options.name: Keep the rules, cut the pours
options.summary: The routed attempt as it stands: every line that has to cross the band does so on the bottom layer, through the power pours. KiCad's DRC passes with 0 errors; 30 items are still unconnected (7 round U201, 3 at the middle cell, 13 supply pads, 7 test points).

images.caption: Before: the east VBAT_IN pour and the VBAT_Q2D pour on B.Cu
The attempt: the same pours with the middle cell's lines cut through them
U201 and U202: the thin lines are joins still open
Middle cell: three joins still open

measures.label: KiCad DRC errors, board's own rules
VBAT_IN, J901 to Q202 (all layers, 85 C)
VBAT_Q2D, R201 to Q203 and Q204 (all layers)
VBAT_D, FET tabs to R201 (outer layers)

gains: Most of the board is connected today: 181 of 211 open items closed
costs: VBAT_Q2D up 82 %, the east VBAT_IN leg up 28 %, OUT4 up 30 %: on the 60 A path and a 10 A output
The outer-layer pours are in pieces; the current leans on the inner layers and the vias at the FET tabs
U201's cluster still does not route on one layer without re-placing R204 to R207

options.name: Signal tracks on top under the GND bar
options.summary:
Change one rule in `node60.kicad_dru`: under the GND busbar only, mask-covered signal tracks may run on F.Cu. Battery nets and other nets' pours stay excluded there, and the VBAT_IN bar's rule does not change. Then route again. The bar is at GND and stands 0.6 mm above the solder mask; the worst case of a fault there is a signal shorted to GND.

Not routed yet, so there are no numbers for it: the facts above show the pour-free way it opens.

images.caption: The pours a route under this rule would leave as they are

measures.label: KiCad DRC errors, board's own rules

gains: A second layer exactly where the board has one: y 61 to 80, with U201 and U202 in it
A way to the middle cell that cuts no power pour
U201's nets cross by a via pair; R204 to R207 can stay
costs: Signal copper 0.6 mm under a bare copper bar, kept apart by solder mask and air: a rule of DEC-025's reading relaxed
The GND pour on F.Cu under the bar is cut by those tracks (it carries no supply current: the bar does)
About an hour of router time to route again, and the same hand work on what it leaves

options.name: 8 layers
options.summary: Two more signal layers under everything. The stackup, the plan's layer roles and DEC-027 change; the placement can stay.

measures.label: KiCad DRC errors, board's own rules

gains: No signal needs a power layer or the space under a bar
What you named as the fallback in D17
costs: $124 more per 5 boards at JLCPCB's quote
DEC-027, the stackup, the via preset and every plane model are redone

recommendation.why:
**B.** It gives the band a second signal layer for the price of one rule, and the fault it risks is a signal touching ground, not battery. A is measured and costs too much on the 60 A path to accept as it is. C works but changes the stackup for a problem one rule solves.

If you take B, the edit is yours to make or to tell me plainly to make: replace the rule "F.Cu under the GND busbar: GND only" with one that disallows other nets' zones there and tracks of the PWR_BATT class, and `prove_rules.py` gets the matching cases. I then route again from main's prepared board.

answer: Reply with A, B or C, or a change to one. For B, say whether I should make the rule edit.
